title: Local topology, entropy compactness and path-space estimates

items.title: Finite-spin product and local topologies
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, a finite nonempty alphabet $S$ with the discrete topology, and a bijective enumeration $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ of $\mathbb Z^d$. Let $\Omega=S^{\mathbb Z^d}$ be the set of all configurations $\sigma:\mathbb Z^d\to S$ with the product topology, the smallest topology that makes each coordinate map $\sigma\mapsto\sigma_x$ continuous. For a finite set $F\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and assignment $a\in S^F$, the cylinder set determined by $(F,a)$ is $[F,a]=\{\sigma\in\Omega:\sigma|_F=a\}$. The cylinder sigma-algebra $\mathcal C$ is generated by these sets.

For each finite $F$, let $\pi_F:\Omega\to S^F$ be restriction to $F$. A probability measure $\rho$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal C)$ is a countably additive map $\mathcal C\to[0,1]$ with $\rho(\varnothing)=0$ and $\rho(\Omega)=1$. Its finite-coordinate pushforward is the measure on all subsets of $S^F$ defined by $(\pi_F)_*\rho(B):=\rho(\pi_F^{-1}(B))$; the preimage is a finite union of cylinders and belongs to $\mathcal C$. For probability measures $\mu_n,\mu$ on this space, local weak convergence $\mu_n\to_{\mathrm{loc}}\mu$ means that $(\pi_F)_*\mu_n(B)\to(\pi_F)_*\mu(B)$ for every finite $F\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and every $B\subseteq S^F$. Equivalently, all finite-coordinate cylinder probabilities converge. The cylinder sigma-algebra is shown below in a local result to equal the Borel sigma-algebra, with local weak convergence equal to ordinary weak convergence on this space.
items.strategy: Definition of the finite-spin product topology, cylinder sets, and local weak convergence.

items.title: Locally finite counting measures and vague topology
items.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$. Let $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d)$ be the $\sigma$-algebra generated by the Euclidean open sets, and understand all measures below as defined on $(\mathbb R^d,\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d))$. A measure here is a countably additive map from $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d)$ to $[0,\infty]$ that assigns $0$ to the empty set. A locally finite counting measure on $\mathbb R^d$ is a measure of the form $\xi=\sum_{r\in I}\delta_{x_r}$, where $I$ is finite or countable, repetitions among the points $x_r\in\mathbb R^d$ are allowed, and every compact set contains only finitely many listed points, counting repetitions. The empty sum is allowed and is the zero measure. For a Borel set $B$, $\xi(B)$ is the number of listed points in $B$, with multiplicity. Write $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lf}}(\mathbb R^d)$ for the set of these measures. For $x\in\mathbb R^d$, the point mass $\delta_x$ assigns mass $1$ to a Borel set containing $x$ and mass $0$ otherwise.

For any continuous compactly supported $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ and $\xi=\sum_{r\in I}\delta_{x_r}$, define $\int f\,d\xi:=\sum_{r:x_r\in\operatorname{supp}f}f(x_r)$, where $\operatorname{supp}f$ is the closure of $\{x:f(x)\ne0\}$. This sum is finite by local finiteness, counts multiplicities, and is independent of the listing because $\xi$ fixes the multiplicity at every point. For the zero measure it is $0$.

The vague topology on $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lf}}(\mathbb R^d)$ is the coarsest topology for which $\xi\mapsto\int f\,d\xi$ is continuous for every nonnegative continuous compactly supported function $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$. Thus $\xi_n\to_{\mathrm v}\xi$ exactly when $\int f\,d\xi_n\to\int f\,d\xi$ for every such $f$.

Given a probability space $(\Theta,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)$, meaning that $\mathcal A$ is a $\sigma$-algebra on $\Theta$ and $\mathbb P$ is a countably additive probability measure on $\mathcal A$ with $\mathbb P(\Theta)=1$, a random locally finite counting measure is an $(\mathcal A,\mathcal B_{\mathrm v})$-measurable map $\Xi:\Theta\to\Gamma_{\mathrm{lf}}(\mathbb R^d)$, where $\mathcal B_{\mathrm v}:=\sigma\{U:U\text{ is open in the vague topology just defined}\}$. We require that, for every bounded Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, the evaluation $\Xi(B):\Theta\to[0,\infty)$ given by $\Xi(B)(\theta)=\Xi(\theta)(B)$ is $\mathcal A$-measurable; it is finite by local finiteness. Write $\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}$ for integration with respect to $\mathbb P$. A sequence $(\Xi_n)$ of such measures on a common probability space uses this same domain and target for every $n$. If $K$ is compact, its local counts are uniformly integrable on $K$ when

$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_n\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}\!\left[\Xi_n(K)\mathbf1_{\{\Xi_n(K)>R\}}\right]=0.$$

This is the count-tail condition used when an argument needs control of unbounded observables supported in $K$. The definition asserts no convergence of expectations without the exact test-function, support, and tail hypotheses of the result being applied.
items.strategy: Definition of locally finite counting measures, vague convergence, and a local-count uniform-integrability condition.

items.title: Finite-state generator chain
items.statement:
Let $E=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ for a finite integer $m\ge1$. A rate matrix on $E$ is a real matrix $L=(L_{ij})_{i,j\in E}$ such that $L_{ij}\ge0$ for $i
e j$ and $\sum_{j\in E}L_{ij}=0$ for every $i$. Write $\lambda_i=\sum_{j
e i}L_{ij}$, so $L_{ii}=-\lambda_i$. The row convention acts on a column observable $f:E	o\mathbb R$ by $(Lf)(i)=\sum_jL_{ij}f(j)$; a row probability vector evolves by right multiplication.

Fix an initial probability vector $
u=(
u_i)_{i\in E}$, meaning $
u_i\ge0$ and $\sum_{i\in E}
u_i=1$; initial law $
u$ means $\mathbb P(Y_0=i)=
u_i$ for every $i\in E$. Put $q=\max_i\lambda_i$. If $q=0$, then $L=0$ and set $N_t=0$ for every $t\ge0$ and let the associated realization be the constant process $X_t=Y_0$ with $Y_0\sim
u$. If $q>0$, put $R=I+L/q$, a stochastic matrix. A uniformized realization consists of a probability space carrying a discrete-time Markov sequence $(Y_n)_{n\ge0}$ with initial law $
u$ and transition matrix $R$, and independent random variables $(W_n)_{n\ge1}$ that are independent of the entire sequence $Y$ and satisfy $\mathbb P(W_n>u)=e^{-qu}$ for $u\ge0$. Here a discrete-time Markov sequence with transition matrix $R$ means that
$$\mathbb P(A\cap\{Y_{n+1}=j\})=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A R_{Y_nj}]$$
for every $n\ge0$, $j\in E$, and $A\in\sigma(Y_0,\ldots,Y_n)$. Each $W_n$ therefore has the exponential distribution of rate $q$; in particular its mean is $q^{-1}$. Require $\sum_{n\ge1}W_n=+\infty$ almost surely. Put $T_0=0$, $T_n=\sum_{k=1}^nW_k$, and, on this probability-one event, $N_t=\max\{n:T_n\le t\}$ and $X_t=Y_{N_t}$. On its null complement set $N_t=0$ and $X_t=Y_0$. The construction filtration is $\mathcal F_t=\sigma(N_s,X_s:0\le s\le t)$; it records event counts and states through time $t$ and is not completed or made right-continuous by this definition.

This uniformized construction permits reducible rate matrices and states with zero exit rate. Under the Axiom of Choice, [[lem-csm-frontier-finite-generator-chain-existence]] proves that every finite rate matrix and initial law admit such a realization and that its conditional transition matrices are $e^{tL}:=\sum_{n=0}^\infty t^nL^n/n!$.
items.strategy: Definition of the finite rate-matrix row convention and its uniformized process and filtration.

items.title: Finite-horizon L2 maximal bound for càdlàg martingales
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T\ge0$, let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space, and let $(\mathcal F_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be an increasing family of sub-$\sigma$-algebras of $\mathcal F$. Let $(M_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be a family of real random variables such that each $M_t$ is $\mathcal F_t$-measurable, $\mathbb E[M_t^2]<\infty$, $M_0=0$, and $\mathbb E[M_t\mid\mathcal F_s]=M_s$ almost surely for every $0\le s\le t\le T$. Suppose it has càdlàg paths almost surely, meaning there is a measurable event $\Omega_0\in\mathcal F$ with $\mathbb P(\Omega_0)=1$ such that, for every $\omega\in\Omega_0$, the path $t\mapsto M_t(\omega)$ is right-continuous on $[0,T)$ and has a finite left limit at every $t\in(0,T]$. Define
$$
D_T=\bigcup_{n\ge0}\{kT/2^n:0\le k\le2^n\},\qquad S_T=\sup_{t\in D_T}|M_t|.
$$
Then $S_T$ is measurable and agrees with the pathwise supremum $\sup_{0\le t\le T}|M_t|$ on $\Omega_0$, and
$$
\mathbb E[S_T^2]\le4\,\mathbb E[|M_T|^2].
$$
items.strategy: First-crossing tail bound on finite dyadic grids, followed by the càdlàg monotone limit.

items.title: Finite relative-entropy chain rule and event grouping
items.statement:
Let $I,J$ be finite nonempty sets, let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on $I\times J$ (a probability vector $p$ on a finite nonempty set $H$ is a function $p:H\to[0,1]$ with $\sum_{z\in H}p(z)=1$), and assume $Q(x,y)>0$ for every $(x,y)$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on a finite set with $q$ strictly positive, define
$$D(p\|q)=\sum_{z:p(z)>0}p(z)\ln\frac{p(z)}{q(z)},$$
with zero-mass terms omitted. For $C\subseteq I\times J$, write $P(C)=\sum_{z\in C}P(z)$ and $Q(C)=\sum_{z\in C}Q(z)$. Define the first-coordinate marginals by $P_X(x)=\sum_{y\in J}P(x,y)$ and $Q_X(x)=\sum_{y\in J}Q(x,y)$. For $x$ with $P_X(x)>0$, define $P_{Y|x}(y)=P(x,y)/P_X(x)$; define $Q_{Y|x}(y)=Q(x,y)/Q_X(x)$ for every $x$, since strict positivity of $Q$ gives $Q_X(x)>0$. These are probability vectors on $J$; terms weighted by $P_X(x)=0$ are omitted. Then
$$D(P\|Q)=D(P_X\|Q_X)+\sum_{x:P_X(x)>0}P_X(x)D(P_{Y|x}\|Q_{Y|x}).$$
For every subset $C\subseteq I\times J$, grouping the atoms into $C$ and its complement cannot increase relative entropy:
$$D(P\|Q)\ge d(P(C)\|Q(C)),\qquad d(a\|b)=a\ln\frac ab+(1-a)\ln\frac{1-a}{1-b},$$
with zero-weight terms omitted. For the empty or full event, the binary divergence is $0$, and the grouping bound reduces to $D(P\|Q)\ge0$, with equality exactly when $P=Q$. For a nonempty proper event $C$, equality holds exactly when, on each of $C$ and $C^c$ having positive $P$-mass, the conditional probability vectors of $P$ and $Q$ agree.
items.strategy: Expand the finite log ratio and group atoms into a two-event partition.

items.title: Cylinder convergence is weak convergence on a finite-spin product
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $S$ be a finite nonempty set with a fixed total order, and fix a bijective enumeration $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ of $\mathbb Z^d$. Put $\Omega=S^{\mathbb Z^d}$, give it the product topology, and let its cylinder sigma-algebra be generated by finite-coordinate assignments. Then the product topology is induced by
$$\rho(\sigma,\eta)=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{-k}\mathbf1_{\{\sigma_{x_k}\ne\eta_{x_k}\}},$$
$\Omega$ is compact, and its Borel sigma-algebra equals the cylinder sigma-algebra. For probability measures $\mu_n,\mu$ on this sigma-algebra, convergence of every finite-coordinate marginal is equivalent to weak convergence, where weak convergence means convergence of integrals of every bounded continuous real function on $\Omega$.
items.strategy: Prove compactness by finite branching, identify the cylinder Borel sigma-algebra, and approximate continuous tests by cylinder functions.

items.title: Uniformization constructs every finite-state rate matrix chain
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $E$ be a nonempty finite set, let $L$ be a rate matrix on $E$ with nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero row sums, and let $\nu$ be an initial probability vector. Then there exists a uniformized realization under the conventions stated below. Its paths are càdlàg and almost surely have only finitely many event times on each bounded interval (nonexplosion), and, for all $0\le s\le t$,
$$\mathbb P(X_t=j\mid\mathcal F_s)=(e^{(t-s)L})_{X_sj}\quad\text{almost surely},$$
where $\mathcal F_s=\sigma(N_u,X_u:0\le u\le s)$ is the construction filtration. In particular, $e^{tL}$ is the transition matrix from any initial state.
items.strategy: Construct the embedded chain and exponential clocks by Ionescu–Tulcea, prove nonexplosion, and derive the matrix-exponential transitions.

items.title: Martingale and predictable bracket for a finite-state chain
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $E$ be finite and nonempty, let $L$ be a rate matrix on $E$, let $X$ be its uniformized realization from the preceding existence result, and let $f:E\to\mathbb R$ be bounded. Put $g=Lf$ and
$$M_t=f(X_t)-f(X_0)-\int_0^t g(X_s)\,ds,\qquad \Gamma_f(i)=L(f^2)(i)-2f(i)Lf(i).$$
For every finite $T$, $(M_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ is a square-integrable martingale relative to the construction filtration, and
$$A_t:=\int_0^t\Gamma_f(X_s)\,ds$$
is its continuous predictable bracket: $A_0=0$, $A$ is increasing and predictable, and $M_t^2-A_t$ is a martingale. The bracket is understood in the continuous predictable increasing compensator convention stated in the proof.
items.strategy: Use semigroup conditional identities and finite small-time second-moment bounds to identify the martingale and bracket.

title: Local topology, entropy compactness and path-space estimates — Examples

items.title: A fixed label vanishes locally while a spatial mark stays random
items.statement:
For each integer $n\ge1$, put $S_n=\{-n,-n+1,\ldots,n-1\}\subset\mathbb Z$ and $L_n=\{1,2,\ldots,2n\}$. Let $\Omega_n$ be the finite set of bijections $\pi:L_n\to S_n$, equipped with its power-set sigma-algebra and probability $\mathbb P_n$ defined by $\mathbb P_n(\{\pi\})=1/(2n)!$ for every $\pi\in\Omega_n$ (and by summing these atom masses on every subset); let $\pi_n$ be the identity random bijection on this probability space. The position of fixed label $1$ is $U_n=\pi_n(1)$, and its point measure is $\Xi_n=\delta_{U_n}$. Give labels $1,\ldots,n$ mark $0$ and labels $n+1,\ldots,2n$ mark $1$. Let $V_n$ be the mark of the particle occupying spatial site $0$. For every nonnegative continuous compactly supported $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\mathbb P_n\!\left(\left|\int f\,d\Xi_n\right|>\varepsilon\right)\longrightarrow0,$$
while $\mathbb P_n(V_n=0)=\mathbb P_n(V_n=1)=1/2$ for every $n$. The testwise convergence assertion uses the varying-space convention displayed here and requires no coupling between different $n$.
items.strategy: Use a uniform random permutation and exact finite counts to contrast fixed-label and spatial selection.
